plan: Given my value of $20, I need to consider how to maximize my profit in this single round. Since this is a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy if I assume other bidders are also rational and bidding their true value. However, if I can anticipate their bids, I might adjust. With no prior rounds, I'll stick to the dominant strategy of bidding my true value.

This is a single-round auction, so long-term profit maximization simplifies to maximizing profit in this round. The optimal strategy in a second-price auction with independent private values is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it's optimal regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding below my value risks losing a profitable item, while bidding above my value risks winning an item for more than it's worth.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding less risks losing to a lower bid, and bidding more risks overpaying if you win. Since my value is $45, I will bid $45.
